iteration_note: Each exam is administered annually; 10 recorded editions. Edition 1 (2017) is the canonical paper below; editions 2-10 are tracked in the version ledger as they are authored.

agents.I: State the HR diagram, the main sequence, and the Eddington limit.
agents.II: Derive the Eddington luminosity from hydrostatic equilibrium and radiation pressure.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Kippenhahn & Weigert, Stellar Structure and Evolution.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline compact objects (field 236). Trap: must not claim stellar models are unique.

agents.I: State transit vs radial-velocity detection and protoplanetary disks.
agents.II: Derive the transit depth and the RV semi-amplitude from the orbital parameters.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Perryman, The Exoplanet Handbook.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline stellar evolution (field 230). Trap: must not claim a candidate is confirmed without follow-up.

agents.I: State the Lambda-CDM halo paradigm, the stellar-mass-halo-mass relation, and quenching.
agents.II: Derive the stellar-mass-halo-mass relation from abundance matching.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Mo, van den Bosch, White, Galaxy Formation and Evolution.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline cosmology (field 233). Trap: must not claim scaling relations are intrinsic without selection effects.

agents.I: State the Friedmann equations, the CMB power spectrum, and BAO.
agents.II: Derive the Friedmann equation from the Einstein field equations for a homogeneous universe.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Dodelson, Modern Cosmology.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline galaxy physics (field 232). Trap: must not claim Lambda-CDM parameters are final (H0 tension).

agents.I: State the acceleration evidence, quintessence vs Lambda, and screening mechanisms.
agents.II: Derive the growth suppression in modified-gravity theories from the modified Poisson equation.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Copeland et al. 2006 (dark energy review).
agents.IV: Scope: must decline particle dark matter (field 210). Trap: must not claim modified gravity is excluded or confirmed.

agents.I: State synchrotron and inverse-Compton emission; define an AGN.
agents.II: Derive the synchrotron spectral index from the electron energy distribution.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Longair, High Energy Astrophysics.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline cosmology (field 233). Trap: must not claim a single band identifies an emission mechanism.

agents.I: State the neutron-star mass-radius relation and accretion disks.
agents.II: Derive the Eddington-limited accretion luminosity and the disk temperature profile.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Shapiro & Teukolsky, Black Holes, White Dwarfs and Neutron Stars.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline GW detection (field 208). Trap: must not claim the NS equation of state is settled.

agents.I: State ISM phases, the CO-to-H2 conversion, and absorption-line systems.
agents.II: Derive the two-phase ISM equilibrium from heating and cooling balance.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Draine, Physics of the Interstellar and Intergalactic Medium.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline star formation (field 230). Trap: must not claim a tracer traces the whole reservoir linearly.

agents.I: State photometry vs spectroscopy and selection functions.
agents.II: Derive the survey selection function and its effect on luminosity-function estimation.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Massey et al. 2013; SDSS/DESI documentation.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline instrumentation (field 239). Trap: must not claim a survey sample is volume-limited without checking.

agents.I: State telescope optics (diffraction limit), detector noise, and adaptive optics.
agents.II: Derive the diffraction-limited resolution and the signal-to-noise of a CCD observation.
agents.III: Situate the theory: McLean, Electronic Imaging in Astronomy.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline data analysis (field 238). Trap: must not claim higher aperture always resolves fainter sources.

agents.I: State hierarchical Bayesian modeling and periodogram false-alarm probability.
agents.II: Derive the Lomb-Scargle periodogram and its false-alarm probability.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Ivezic et al., Statistics, Data Mining and Machine Learning in Astronomy.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline general statistics (field 34). Trap: must not claim a detected period is real without FAP analysis.

agents.I: State the solar dynamo, the 11-year cycle, and coronal mass ejections.
agents.II: Derive the Parker spiral from the rotating solar wind.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Priest, Solar Magnetohydrodynamics.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline space-weather operations (field 356). Trap: must not claim flare prediction is reliable.

agents.I: State the habitable zone and biosignatures; the Fermi paradox.
agents.II: Derive the habitable-zone boundaries from the stellar luminosity and the runaway-greenhouse limit.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Seager, Exoplanet Atmospheres.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline exoplanet detection (field 231). Trap: must not claim a detection is a biosignature without ruling out abiotic sources.

agents.I: State the lens equation, the Einstein radius, and weak vs strong lensing.
agents.II: Derive the Einstein radius for a point mass and the time-delay formula.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Bartelmann & Schneider 2001.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline cosmological inference (field 233). Trap: must not claim a lens model is unique.

agents.I: State interferometry (uv-plane), aperture synthesis, and resolution limits.
agents.II: Derive the interferometric visibility from the sky brightness and the uv coverage.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Thompson, Moran, Swenson, Interferometry and Synthesis in Radio Astronomy.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline instrument design (field 239). Trap: must not claim a map is artifact-free without calibration.

agents.I: State retrosynthetic analysis and protecting-group strategy.
agents.II: Design a retrosynthetic route to a target molecule and defend each disconnection.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Clayden et al., Organic Chemistry.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline mechanism theory (field 246). Trap: must not claim yields transfer across substrates.

agents.I: State the Hammett equation and isotope effects; define a reaction coordinate.
agents.II: Derive the Hammett equation from the linear free-energy relationship and compute rho.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Anslyn & Dougherty, Modern Physical Organic Chemistry.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline synthesis planning (field 245). Trap: must not claim LFERs hold outside their regime.

agents.I: State crystal-field vs ligand-field theory and oxidation states.
agents.II: Derive the d-orbital splitting in an octahedral field and the resulting electronic configurations.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Housecroft & Sharpe, Inorganic Chemistry.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline catalysis kinetics (field 248). Trap: must not claim d-orbital splitting explains all color.

agents.I: State oxidative addition/reductive elimination and the catalytic cycle.
agents.II: Derive the catalytic cycle of a cross-coupling reaction and its rate law.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Crabtree, The Organometallic Chemistry of the Transition Metals.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline reactor engineering (field 479). Trap: must not claim model-system TOF reflects process performance.

agents.I: State the laws of thermodynamics and chemical potential.
agents.II: Derive the Gibbs-Duhem relation and the phase-equilibrium conditions.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Atkins & de Paula, Physical Chemistry.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline statistical thermodynamics (field 213). Trap: must not claim dG predicts rate.

agents.I: State rate laws, the Arrhenius equation, and potential energy surfaces.
agents.II: Derive the steady-state rate law for a two-step mechanism and the Arrhenius parameters.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Steinfeld, Francisco, Hase, Chemical Kinetics and Dynamics.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline catalysis (field 248). Trap: must not claim an elementary step is first-order without molecularity evidence.

agents.I: State the Born-Oppenheimer approximation, basis sets, and correlation methods (CCSD).
agents.II: Derive the Hartree-Fock equations from the variational principle.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Szabo & Ostlund, Modern Quantum Chemistry.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline DFT (field 216). Trap: must not claim a method is variational unless it is.

agents.I: State force fields vs QM/MM and free-energy perturbation.
agents.II: Derive the free-energy perturbation identity and its convergence properties.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Leach, Molecular Modelling.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline drug scoring (field 341). Trap: must not claim an MM trajectory captures bond breaking.

agents.I: State chromatography resolution and detector limits; calibration curves.
agents.II: Derive the chromatographic resolution equation and the detection-limit formula.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Skoog, Holler, Crouch, Principles of Instrumental Analysis.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline structural biology (field 265). Trap: must not claim detection limit equals quantification limit.

agents.I: State the Nernst equation, cyclic voltammetry, and the double layer.
agents.II: Derive the Nernst equation from electrochemical potentials and the CV peak separation.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Bard & Faulkner, Electrochemical Methods.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline battery engineering (field 494). Trap: must not claim a CV feature identifies a mechanism without scan-rate analysis.

agents.I: State the Jablonski diagram, quantum yield, and triplet-state roles.
agents.II: Derive the Stern-Volmer quenching equation and the quantum-yield definition.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Turro, Ramamurthy, Scaiano, Modern Molecular Photochemistry.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline spectroscopy (field 253). Trap: must not treat excited-state reactivity as ground-state-like.

agents.I: State host-guest binding, the chelate effect, and self-assembly.
agents.II: Derive the binding isotherm for a 1:1 host-guest complex and the chelate enhancement.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Steed & Atwood, Supramolecular Chemistry.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline polymer chemistry (field 257). Trap: must not claim a binding constant is a selectivity constant.

agents.I: State step vs chain growth and living polymerization dispersity.
agents.II: Derive the Carothers equation and the dispersity of a living polymerization.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Odian, Principles of Polymerization.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline polymer physics (field 222). Trap: must not claim properties are set solely by the monomer.

agents.I: State synthesis-structure-property relations and the sol-gel route.
agents.II: Derive the sol-gel hydrolysis-condensation kinetics and the resulting pore structure.
agents.III: Situate the theory: West, Solid State Chemistry and Its Applications.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline condensed-matter physics (field 216). Trap: must not claim a powder's property equals the bulk material's.

agents.I: State Langmuir adsorption, the Sabatier principle, and turnover frequency.
agents.II: Derive the Langmuir isotherm and the two-site Langmuir-Hinshelwood rate law.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Chorkendorff & Niemantsverdriet, Concepts of Modern Catalysis and Kinetics.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline homogeneous catalysis (field 248). Trap: must not claim UHV measurements transfer to ambient conditions.

agents.I: State activity-based probes, covalent labeling, and chemical genetics.
agents.II: Derive the activity-based probe labeling kinetics and its specificity design.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Schreiber 1998 (chemical genetics); Cravatt et al.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline cell biology (field 264). Trap: must not claim a probe is specific without competition controls.

agents.I: State SAR/QSAR, lead optimization, and pharmacophores.
agents.II: Derive a QSAR model and its predictive-validity metric for a lead series.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Wermuth, The Practice of Medicinal Chemistry.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline clinical pharmacology (field 335). Trap: must not claim in-vitro potency predicts in-vivo efficacy.

agents.I: State the 12 principles, atom economy, and the E-factor.
agents.II: Derive the E-factor and atom economy of a synthesis and identify the green metric trade-offs.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Anastas & Warner, Green Chemistry: Theory and Practice.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline ecotoxicology (field 368). Trap: must not claim a solvent switch alone makes a process green.

agents.I: State the central dogma and transcriptional regulation; define a transcription factor.
agents.II: Derive the Michaelis-Menten-like model of transcription-factor binding and activation.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Alberts et al., Molecular Biology of the Cell.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline chromatin (field 269). Trap: must not claim mRNA level equals protein activity.

agents.I: State signal transduction cascades and second messengers.
agents.II: Derive the ultrasensitive response of a kinase cascade and its switch-like behavior.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Lodish et al., Molecular Cell Biology.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline metabolism (field 279). Trap: must not claim a pathway diagram is the whole story.

agents.I: State cryo-EM/X-ray resolution and PDB validation.
agents.II: Derive the Fourier-synthesis map from diffraction intensities and the phase problem.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Rhodes, Crystallography Made Crystal Clear.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline folding dynamics (field 267). Trap: must not claim a static structure explains dynamic function.

agents.I: State Michaelis-Menten kinetics and the catalytic cycle.
agents.II: Derive the Michaelis-Menten equation from the steady-state assumption.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Fersht, Structure and Mechanism in Protein Science.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline metabolic flux (field 279). Trap: must not claim Vmax/Km alone determines in-vivo rates.

agents.I: State the folding funnel and intrinsically disordered regions.
agents.II: Derive the two-state folding kinetics and the Arrhenius-like rate of folding.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Dill & MacCallum 2012.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline structure determination (field 265). Trap: must not claim a predicted structure is a validated experiment.

agents.I: State Mendelian inheritance, mutation classes, and loss vs gain of function.
agents.II: Derive the segregation ratios for a monohybrid cross and the LOD score for linkage.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Strachan & Read, Human Molecular Genetics.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline population genetics (field 292). Trap: must not claim a variant is pathogenic without functional evidence.

agents.I: State histone modifications, DNA methylation, and chromatin states.
agents.II: Derive the read-write model of histone-mark propagation and its bistability.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Allis & Jenuwein 2016.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline transcription (field 263). Trap: must not claim marks are permanent or solely heritable.

agents.I: State splicing, splice variants, and noncoding RNAs.
agents.II: Derive the splicing-consensus scoring model and the branch-point selection rules.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Sharp 2009; Cech & Steitz 2014.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline transcription (field 263). Trap: must not claim every lncRNA is functional.

agents.I: State replication fidelity and repair pathways (NER, BER, MMR, HR).
agents.II: Derive the error rate of DNA replication from polymerase fidelity and proofreading.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Friedberg et al., DNA Repair and Mutagenesis.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline cell cycle (field 272). Trap: must not claim a repair pathway is error-free.

agents.I: State cyclin-CDK control, checkpoints, and the hallmarks of cancer.
agents.II: Derive the bistable switch model of the G1/S checkpoint.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Hanahan & Weinberg 2011; Morgan, The Cell Cycle.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline clinical oncology (field 313). Trap: must not claim a cell line represents a patient tumor.

agents.I: State potency definitions, the niche, and iPSC reprogramming.
agents.II: Derive the symmetric/asymmetric division model and the resulting clone-size distribution.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Yamanaka 2006 (iPSC).
agents.IV: Scope: must decline development (field 274). Trap: must not claim a marker alone defines a stem cell.

agents.I: State morphogen gradients, Hox patterning, and organizers.
agents.II: Derive the French-flag morphogen model and its readout precision.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Gilbert, Developmental Biology.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline stem-cell potency (field 273). Trap: must not claim a knockout phenotype is gene-autonomous.

agents.I: State growth phases, the cell envelope, and antibiotic mechanisms.
agents.II: Derive the Monod growth equation and the chemostat steady state.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Madigan et al., Brock Biology of Microorganisms.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline clinical infections (field 320). Trap: must not claim culture-based ID is complete.

agents.I: State lytic vs lysogenic cycles and viral genome types.
agents.II: Derive the eclipse/rise/plateau kinetics of a one-step viral growth curve.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Flint et al., Principles of Virology.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline clinical disease (field 320). Trap: must not claim a vaccine strain covers all variants.

agents.I: State V(D)J recombination, MHC restriction, and memory responses.
agents.II: Derive the diversity estimate from V(D)J combinatorial and junctional mechanisms.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Murphy & Weaver, Janeway's Immunobiology.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline clinical immunology (field 321). Trap: must not claim antibody presence implies protection.

agents.I: State the lipid bilayer, transport classes, and the electrochemical gradient.
agents.II: Derive the Goldman-Hodgkin-Katz equation for the resting membrane potential.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Hille, Ion Channels of Excitable Membranes.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline signaling (field 264). Trap: must not claim transporter direction is set by concentration alone.

agents.I: State glycolysis/TCA/oxidative phosphorylation and redox balance.
agents.II: Derive the proton-motive force and the ATP yield of oxidative phosphorylation.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Berg, Tymoczko, Gatto, Stryer, Biochemistry.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline clinical endocrinology (field 316). Trap: must not claim metabolite abundance reflects flux.

agents.I: State the secretory pathway, vesicle trafficking (SNAREs), and membrane contact sites.
agents.II: Derive the SNARE-mediated fusion kinetics and the vesicle-budding COPII cycle.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Bonifacino & Glick 2004.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline membrane transport (field 278). Trap: must not claim localization predicts function without perturbation.
